fullPassage: When social scientists discovered that the magnitude of income inequality in a country or region predicted some outcomes that a family's average income did not, economists invented an index of income inequality called the Gini coefficient. A Gini coefficient of 0 means that everyone in the society has the same income; a coefficient of 1.0 means that one family earns all the income. The Gini coefficient can also be used to index inequality in total wealth. The coefficients in most contemporary societies range from 0.3 to 0.6. Canada, Japan, and the Scandinavian countries have low coefficients (less than 0.3); South Africa, Brazil, Nigeria, and China have the highest (from 0.4 to 0.6). The Gini coefficient for the United States in 2013 was a moderately high 0.45, compared with 0.38 in 1950, which implies that 10 percent of Americans in 2013 owned more than two-thirds of the country's wealth. The Gini coefficient for the United States was much lower two hundred years earlier when most families owned a house and livestock, and a college education was a less important requirement for accumulating wealth. The currently high level of inequality is accompanied by an imbalance in the degree of influence on legislation. Two social scientists report in Perspectives on Politics that between 1981 and 2002, close to one-half of the laws Congress passed were favored by a small proportion of very wealthy Americans. By contrast, only 18 percent of the proposals a majority of the public favored, but the wealthy opposed, became law.

A Gini coefficient of 0 means that everyone in the society has the same income; a coefficient of 1.0 means that one family earns all the income. Canada, Japan, and the Scandinavian countries have low coefficients (less than 0.3); South Africa, Brazil, Nigeria, and China have the highest (from 0.4 to 0.6). The Gini coefficient for the United States in 2013 was a moderately high 0.45, compared with 0.38 in 1950, which implies that 10 percent of Americans in 2013 owned more than two-thirds of the country's wealth. The Gini coefficient for the United States was much lower two hundred years earlier when most families owned a house and livestock, and a college education was a less important requirement for accumulating wealth. det.tip: 앞뒤 문장이 서로 반대되는 비율(부유층 선호 법의 통과 vs 대중 선호 제안의 낮은 통과율)을 보여줄 때는 대조 연결어(By contrast)가 와야 한다.

questions.passage: When social scientists discovered that the magnitude of income inequality in a country or region predicted some outcomes that a family's average income did not, economists invented an index of income inequality called the Gini coefficient. A Gini coefficient of 0 means that everyone in the society has the same income; a coefficient of 1.0 means that one family earns all the income. The Gini coefficient can also be used to index inequality in total wealth. The coefficients in most contemporary societies range from 0.3 to 0.6. Canada, Japan, and the Scandinavian countries have low coefficients (less than 0.3); South Africa, Brazil, Nigeria, and China have the highest (from 0.4 to 0.6). The Gini coefficient for the United States in 2013 was a moderately high 0.45, compared with 0.38 in 1950, which implies that 10 percent of Americans in 2013 owned more than two-thirds of the country's wealth. The Gini coefficient for the United States was much lower two hundred years earlier when most families owned a house and livestock, and a college education was a less important requirement for accumulating wealth. The currently high level of inequality is accompanied by an imbalance in the degree of influence on legislation. Two social scientists report in Perspectives on Politics that between 1981 and 2002, close to one-half of the laws Congress passed were favored by a small proportion of very wealthy Americans. By contrast, only 18 percent of the proposals a majority of the public favored, __________ the wealthy opposed, became law.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 대중 다수가 선호했지만, '그러나' 부유층이 반대한 제안 중에서는 18퍼센트만이 법이 되었다.
det.analysis:
① and: '그리고'는 단순 나열 접속사라 두 주체의 반대되는 입장을 드러내지 못해 부적절❌
② but: 대중이 선호한 것과 부유층이 반대한 것이 서로 상반되는 내용을 연결하는 접속사로 적절✅
③ so: '그래서'는 인과관계를 나타내 대중의 선호가 부유층의 반대를 일으켰다는 어색한 의미가 되어 부적절❌
④ since: '~ 때문에/이후로'는 인과·시간 관계라 단순 대조 의미와 어긋나 부적절❌
det.tip: 같은 제안에 대해 두 주체(대중과 부유층)가 서로 반대 입장을 보일 때는 등위접속사 but으로 대조시켜야 한다.
